correctness.rationale: Sixteen distinct nonempty traces require at least five code vertices since 2^4−1=15. Independent enumeration (python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 4) used the six specified differences, compared all sixteen closed-neighborhood traces for each of the 4368 five-subsets, and found exactly the 96 distinct sets obtained by taking the three other vertices of the root's parity coset plus an edge of its open neighborhood. An independent exchange construction indexed the accepted sets by their four-element subsets; it gave degree two at each vertex and precisely sixteen connected groups of size six. There is also a direct check that distinct roots cannot exchange: for distinct cosets their cores are disjoint and an adjacent pair meets either specified coset in at most one vertex. To have intersection four would require both extra vertices of each code in the opposite core, so this is impossible. In the same coset distinct cores intersect in two, so intersection four would require a common adjacent pair in both root neighborhoods. For each nonzero parity-coset displacement (2,0), (0,2), (2,2), the two common neighbors are opposite and nonadjacent. For a fixed root the six edges of the neighborhood cycle give their line graph, again a six-cycle. These checks use the labeled graph, nonempty traces and unrestricted replacement exactly as specified.
